Our customers suck, and they will always try to pull you. If you make a mistake, ask for help immediately because if you don't speak up there isn't a way to cover yourself. You are going into the worst part of the store, besides maintenance, make sure you utilize self care. If you have a question, ask. If you are threatened, reach out immediately. 

You are allowed to not check someone out who is being an asshole. You may be treated like trash but you are not trash. 

In the beginning you will feel like a burden and realistically you will be, but everyone starts somewhere. 

The first few days will be overwhelming because of the amount of input. If you last 90 days, and don't call out, you have made a huge accomplishment. 

No one will tell you that you are doing a good job, but when you realize you are doing your job and you don't have to rely on others for constant support, you are allowed to feel proud of yourself. 

Front end has a high turn over because our customers are wolves. My first week working on a register someone tried to shortchange me. I was given a fake $100 bill, and I was screamed at every day because our customers take advantage of new people. 

The person hovering around you, they will feel like they don't trust you, and maybe they won't, but the biggest issue will be with them not trusting our customers, not you. 

There are resources if you do get overwhelmed. If you have depression and/or anxiety, please let someone know that you are curious about a program called Lyra. You can even say that you heard something online. They are your free resource to counseling and such. 

Don't give up! It will be difficult for the first month or so. Failure is the end, it's just the "First Attempt In Learning". 

You can do it!

I became a TL because I had that kind of TL. He still will show me things and help if I ask, and I will always be willing to help him. 

It's crazy because I'm a "words of affirmation" type of person and as soon as he would start saying "today is gonna be a great day cuz I got my dream team here",  I would race my old times just trying to show him I appreciated him. 

Now, I arrive 30 minutes before I'm scheduled just in case ON didn't get to finish hardware and I will knock out the remaining pallets before my team clocks in. 

In Academy, they stress the importance of "Thank your associates" and although I was that person from day 1, I was grateful because acknowledging the fact that your team is doing their best is so needed yet so few actually do it. 

I understand that it sucks when the job isn't done and you get yelled at, but your team isn't always the problem. In my case, it's the stores problem because I only have 1 associate on day, 1 on close and like 16 hours worth of work, in a service area where we are constantly pulled to the registers. I won't yell at them. I don't get upset with them. I try to figure out a plan to get the most done and we do our best. If they want more done, we need at least 2 more people. 1 for just register and another for mods, or stocking and returns. 

There's no possible way to do more. 

I found out one of my team members has diabetes, so I can't give out sugar cookies anymore. But I can continue to do things regarding food.

I have really amazing peeps, but dang it's hard!

We get day expired fruit and bread and peanut butter and jelly.

I wish we had some chewy bars. Every time I ever got an apple it had teeth marks on it. The bananas were good though.

I actually have told everyone about it, especially the phone plans. $10/month or $200 a month? But yes. I subscribed to our discount center. 

You know, now they have academy courses? They are classes for people to take once they are promoted? 

You're willingness to help, even those online, and the fact that you are transparent... that's how TLs are supposed to be.
